newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Berisha draws biggest crowd of campaign.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Berisha draws biggest crowd of campaign.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha, drawing the biggest crowd of his election campaign, told 6,000 cheering people in the port of Durres on Sunday that his Democratic Party would lead them into Europe.
"We are going to win the elections because we are voting for the future and we are going to lead our country into Europe," he told the enthusiastic crowd jammed into a sports hall.

Berisha, who spoke and answered written questions for about an hour, was frequently interrupted by people chanting his name and by applause from supporters waving Albanian flags and blue-and-white Democratic Party banners.
Reporters who have covered some of Berisha's other campaign rallies ahead of elections on June 29, said the Durres crowd was by far the largest.
Berisha, clearly fired by the crowd's enthusiasm, accused the rival Socialist Party of backing the salvation committees that hold sway in Vlore and other parts of the south.
He blamed them for the lawlessness that has persisted in Albania since rioting in February and March after dubious pyramid investment schemes collapsed and said they had chosen "to act like rebels."
"I have chosen the right way to fight them, in the political way," he said.

The Socialist Party, reformed heirs to the communists who ruled the Balkan nation with an iron hand for four decades, said they would hold a rally in a Tirana soccer field on Tuesday to launch their election campaign.
"We invite...all those who oppose the dictatorship and the violation of the free votes of the people, all those who want real democracy to win," the Socialist daily Zeri i Popullit said.
The Socialist-led opposition pulled out of Albania's third parliamentary elections in May 26 last year, accusing Berisha's Democratic Party of rigging the poll and intimidating voters.
Albania is now run by a nine-party National Reconciliation government.

Socialist chairman Fatos Nano, who was pardoned by Berisha after jails were broken into during the rioting and looting in March, is expected at the rally for his first public appearance since he was arrested four years ago on charges of embezzlement.
